title: Why a Zscaler Terraform plan shows no diff, or a replacement: diff suppression, ForceNew and code-only checks

prose.text: Which arguments force replacement (ForceNew), conflict with each other, or are validated against a fixed list is generated per resource by `node scripts/kb.mjs surface <resource name>`. This collects the behavior the schema listing does not show.

prose.heading: Multi-line text in the ZIA provider

prose.text: {{zia-multiline-functions}} {{zia-multiline-scope}} {{zia-multiline-cannot-clear}} The URL Filtering case is [[zia.api.url-filtering-wire:tf-description-diff-suppression]], and the ZTC provider carries the same pair of helpers ([[cloud-connector.terraform.provider-behavior:multiline-diff-suppress-ignores-clears]]). Whether the ZIA API itself normalizes whitespace in these fields is open {{gap:api-whitespace-normalization}}.

prose.heading: Other suppressed diffs in the ZPA provider

prose.text: {{zpa-coordinates}} The connector group case is [[zpa.app-connectors.connector-groups:tf-coordinates-six-decimals]]. Service Edge group membership is ignored unless configured: [[zpa.private-service-edges.terraform:service-edges-diff-suppressed-when-unset]].

VPN credential identity fields force a new credential ([[zia.traffic-forwarding.vpn-credentials:immutable]], [[zia.traffic-forwarding.vpn-credentials:psk-required]]). Provider v4.4.6 removed ForceNew from `select_connector_close_to_app` ([[zpa.app-segments.settings:forcenew-removed]], [[zpa.browser-access.tooling:tf-select-connector-not-forcenew]]). The Cloud App Control rule type is not ForceNew in the schema ([[zia.terraform.cloud-app-control-rule:tf-rule-type-optional]]). What a replaced policy rule does to rule order is open {{gap:replaced-rule-order}}.

prose.heading: Checks that live in code, not the schema

prose.text: A Browser Access app that sets `certificate_id` with `ext_label` or `ext_domain` is rejected in the resource code ([[zpa.browser-access.tooling:tf-certificate-conflicts-ext-fields]]); server groups check servers against dynamic discovery on create and update ([[zpa.server-groups.discovery-mode:tf-dsd-off-needs-servers]]); a credential rule needs exactly one of credential or pool ([[zpa.terraform.policy-rule-writes:credential-update-restores-remote-association]]); Service Edge grace distance fields go together ([[zpa.private-service-edges.terraform:zpa-terraform-grace]]). A provider validator shows what the provider accepts, which can differ from the API, as with BRAVE ([[zia.terraform.url-filtering-rules:validator-omits-brave]]).

checks.do: When a ZIA description or notes change does not plan, whether the new value is empty, which the diff suppression always treats as no change.
Whether the argument being changed is marked force_new in the generated surface for that resource, before applying a change to a rule or credential.

zia-multiline-functions.statement: The ZIA provider's `normalizeMultiLineString` trims the text and each line, doubles every `$` (`$` becomes `$$`) and appends a newline; `noChangeInMultiLineText` returns true (no difference) whenever the new text is empty, and otherwise compares the two normalized values.

quotes: func noChangeInMultiLineText(k, oldText, newText string, d *schema.ResourceData) bool { if newText == "" { return true }

zia-multiline-scope.statement: In the ZIA provider, 39 resource files attach `noChangeInMultiLineText` as a DiffSuppressFunc, on `description` in 37 attachments and also on notification text fields such as `html_message`, `plain_text_message`, `subject` and `rule_text`; the URL Filtering rule pairs it with `normalizeMultiLineString` as its StateFunc.

quotes: StateFunc:        normalizeMultiLineString, // Ensures correct format before storing in Terraform state
DiffSuppressFunc: noChangeInMultiLineText,  // Prevents unnecessary Terraform diffs

zia-multiline-scope.conditions: Counted at the pin with a search for "DiffSuppressFunc: noChangeInMultiLineText" across non-test files under zia/, which matched 39 resource files; the attribute names come from the schema keys above each match. The quoted URL Filtering lines are one instance.

zia-multiline-cannot-clear.statement: On those ZIA attributes a value cannot be cleared by removing it or setting it to an empty string: the empty new value is suppressed as no difference, so no update is planned.
zia-multiline-cannot-clear.conditions: Follows from the diff-suppress function returning true for empty new text; not shown by a provider test.

zpa-coordinates.statement: The ZPA provider's `DiffSuppressFuncCoordinate` treats two coordinates as equal when they match after rounding to six decimal places, and it is attached to `latitude` and `longitude` on the App Connector group, Service Edge group and Private Cloud group resources.

api-whitespace-normalization.title: Whether ZIA normalizes whitespace in description and notes fields
api-whitespace-normalization.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "The API normalizes whitespace and line endings server-side; Terraform suppresses spurious diffs." The provider code shows only that the provider normalizes and suppresses; no source shows what the API stores.
api-whitespace-normalization.blocks: explaining a drift between configured and stored text

replaced-rule-order.title: What replacing a policy rule through ForceNew does to rule order
replaced-rule-order.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Policy Access rules - reauth_timeout and reauth_idle_timeout are both ForceNew. Changing a session/idle timeout on an existing rule requires destroy-recreate - the API refuses in-place updates. This can renumber nearby rules." The generated surface shows the two arguments as force_new on the v1 timeout rule resource; no source shows that the API refuses an in-place update or how the recreated rule is ordered.
replaced-rule-order.blocks: planning a timeout change on a v1 rule in a tenant where rule order matters
